name: Romania
tagline: Saxon fortified churches, painted monasteries, and the largest population of brown bears in Europe.
summary: Romania is a Latin language surrounded by Slavic ones, with a German-founded Transylvania in the middle and an Orthodox monastic north. It has Europe's largest remaining virgin forest, some 6,000 brown bears, and hay meadows farmed by scythe in villages where that never stopped. Bucharest carries the marks of Ceaușescu's demolitions and the Belle Époque city he demolished.

season.note: May and June for hay meadows and wildflowers, September for the light and the food. The Transfăgărășan road opens roughly July to October and is closed by snow the rest of the year. Winter is cold and the Carpathian ski areas are cheap.

getting_around: Trains are slow but reach the Transylvanian towns and the Danube. Buses and minibuses fill the gaps. A car is close to essential for the Saxon villages and the painted monasteries.
food: Sarmale: cabbage rolls with polenta and sour cream
Ciorbă, a sour soup, in dozens of versions
Țuică and pălincă, plum spirits, home-distilled and strong

festivals.name: Easter in Bucovina, with painted eggs

know: Bears are genuinely present in the Carpathians; do not feed them from a car, which is both illegal and how people get hurt.
Village guesthouses (pensiuni) are the best accommodation in the country and cost very little.

regions.name: Transylvania
regions.summary: Saxon fortified churches, walled towns, and the Carpathian ridge behind them.

cities.name: Brașov
cities.summary: A Saxon town under a wooded mountain, with the largest gothic church between Vienna and Istanbul.
highlights: The Black Church, and its collection of Anatolian carpets
Tâmpa mountain, straight up behind the square
Bran and Râșnov castles nearby — the first has little to do with Dracula

experiences.name: A bear hide in the Carpathians
experiences.summary: Licensed hides run by biologists at dusk; Romania holds most of Europe's brown bears and this is the ethical way to see one.

cities.name: Sighișoara
cities.summary: A walled Saxon citadel still lived in, with a clock tower and a covered stairway to a hilltop school.
highlights: The clock tower's figures, turning since 1648
The covered stairway, 175 steps, built so children could get to school in snow
Painted guild houses inside the walls

cities.name: Viscri
cities.summary: A single-street Saxon village with a fortified church, horses on the road, and no through traffic.
highlights: The fortified church, whitewashed, on the UNESCO list
Hay meadows with some of the richest plant diversity in Europe
Guesthouses in restored Saxon houses with blue-painted gates

experiences.name: Haymaking with a scythe
experiences.summary: The meadows are cut by hand because machines would destroy them; in June the villages will show you how and it is harder than it looks.

regions.name: Bucovina & Maramureș
regions.summary: The painted monasteries of the north, and wooden churches with shingle spires.

cities.name: Gura Humorului & the painted monasteries
cities.summary: The base for a group of 15th- and 16th-century monasteries frescoed on the outside walls and still bright.
highlights: Voroneț's blue, a pigment nobody has fully reproduced
Sucevița's Ladder of Virtue, thirty rungs across a wall
Exterior frescoes that have survived five centuries of Carpathian weather

experiences.name: The blue at Voroneț
experiences.summary: A 1547 exterior fresco whose blue has not faded in five hundred winters, and whose recipe is still not known.

cities.name: Săpânța & Maramureș
cities.summary: Wooden churches with tall shingled spires, and a cemetery where every headstone is painted, rhymed and often rude.
highlights: The Merry Cemetery: 800 carved oak crosses with verses about the dead
Wooden churches on the UNESCO list, built without nails
Horse carts, which are transport rather than heritage

regions.name: Bucharest & the Danube Delta
regions.summary: The capital, and Europe's largest wetland where the river reaches the Black Sea.

cities.name: Bucharest
cities.summary: Belle Époque boulevards, communist megastructures, and the second-largest administrative building on earth.
highlights: The Palace of the Parliament, which required demolishing a fifth of the old city
The Village Museum: 300 relocated buildings in a park
Lipscani's bars, in the old merchant quarter

cities.name: Tulcea & the Danube Delta
cities.summary: The gateway to 5,800 square kilometres of reed, channel and lake, with 300 bird species and villages reachable only by boat.
highlights: Pelican colonies, the largest outside Africa
Fishing villages with no road access at all
Fish soup cooked on the boat, in the delta, by the person who caught it

experiences.name: Into the delta by small boat
experiences.summary: The big tour boats stay in the main channels; a local with a small engine gets you into the reed corridors where the birds are.
